summary: Describes Virtual Private LAN Service, a Layer 2 VPN that joins customer sites into one multipoint Ethernet LAN over a provider network. It uses BGP to discover which sites belong together and to set up the connections.

eli5.summary: A company has offices in many cities. VPLS makes them behave as if they were plugged into one big switch. BGP is how the provider's routers find the offices and link them.

questions: how does bgp vpls auto-discovery work
what is a vpls label block
subtitle: How provider routers use BGP to find each other and wire up a multipoint Ethernet LAN across a network.

tldr.problem: A provider wants to join a customer's Ethernet sites in many places into one LAN, without configuring every router with the identity of every other router in that service.
tldr.mechanism: Provider edge routers announce VPLS membership and MPLS labels in a single BGP update, using a Route Target to identify the VPLS and label blocks to hand out labels for many peers at once. They then learn MAC addresses and flood frames like a bridge.
tldr.outcome: One BGP update does both auto-discovery and pseudowire setup. The IESG note says this method and the LDP-based one in RFC 4762 are both called VPLS but are distinct and incompatible.

today: RFC 4761 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 5462, RFC 8395 and RFC 8614; it has not been obsoleted. It remains the definition of BGP-signaled VPLS, which is distinct from and incompatible with the LDP-signaled method in RFC 4762.

sections.title: What VPLS Is For
sections.content:
Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) is a Layer 2 Virtual Private Network where the customer sites are joined by a multipoint Ethernet LAN. The RFC contrasts this with the usual Layer 2 VPNs, which are point-to-point. To the customer, a virtual private LAN appears in almost all respects as an Ethernet LAN, even though the sites may be spread across a metro or wide area.

The service works by gluing several individual LANs together across a packet switched network. It does this by adding MAC address learning, flooding and forwarding in the context of pseudowires that connect the LANs.

This RFC defines the functions needed to offer VPLS, a BGP-based way to auto-discover the endpoints and signal the pseudowires, and how frames travel over tunnels. The IESG note warns that RFC 4762 uses a different method for a similar purpose. Both are called VPLS, but they are distinct and incompatible.
sections.eli5: Imagine several playrooms in different buildings joined so that kids in all of them can chat as if they were in one big room. VPLS is the plumbing that makes the far-apart rooms act like one.

sections.title: The Functional Model
sections.content:
A provider network has P (provider-only) routers and PE (Provider Edge) routers. Customers attach through CE (Customer Edge) devices. The CE is VPLS-unaware: as far as it can tell, it is connected to the other CEs through a Layer 2 switched network, so no change to the CE is needed. PE routers are VPLS-aware. A u-PE is a Layer 2 aggregation device that is also VPLS-aware, and a VE is a VPLS edge device, either a PE or a u-PE.

The RFC assumes the PEs are logically fully meshed with tunnels, which can be IP tunnels such as GRE or MPLS tunnels set up by RSVP-TE or LDP. Every pair of PEs in a VPLS also has a bidirectional pseudowire, so an ingress PE can send straight to the egress PE. Setting up the tunnels themselves is outside this document.

VPLS is a LAN service because CEs in one VPLS interact as if on a LAN. It is private because CEs in different VPLSs cannot interact, and virtual because many VPLSs share one packet switched network. A PE can take part in both VPLS and IP VPNs from RFC 4364 at once, but must keep separate routing storage for each because they use different address family identifiers.
sections.eli5: Each office plugs into the provider's nearest router. The office thinks it is plugged into an ordinary switch and never needs to know about the tunnels underneath.

sections.title: Auto-Discovery and Signaling with BGP
sections.content:
Without auto-discovery, every PE must be configured with every other PE in the VPLS, and every PE must be updated when one is added or removed. With auto-discovery, a PE is configured only with its own VPLS instance. The other PEs are found through BGP.

A BGP Route Target extended community identifies the VPLS. A PE says it belongs to VPLS V by attaching the Route Target to its announcements and accepting announcements that carry the same one. It leaves by withdrawing everything it advertised with that Route Target.

The same BGP Update also does signaling. To create a VPLS, the administrator picks a Route Target. To add a PE, the administrator only chooses a VE ID. The PE generates a Route Distinguisher if none is configured, builds a VPLS NLRI, attaches a Layer2 Info Extended Community and the Route Target, sets itself as BGP next hop, and announces it. When it hears an announcement with the same Route Target from another PE, it knows that PE is a member and sets up its half of the pseudowire.

The RFC states that no MAC addresses are exchanged via BGP. Learning and aging happen in the data plane in each PE. BGP is used only for auto-discovery and label exchange.
sections.eli5: Every office router shouts out a club badge and a list of secret door numbers. Routers wearing the same badge hear each other and connect, so nobody has to hand-write the guest list.

sections.title: Label Blocks, the NLRI and PE Capabilities
sections.content:
Sending a separate BGP update to each of N remote PEs would be wasteful. Instead the RFC introduces label blocks. A block is defined by a label base LB and a VE block size VBS, and is the contiguous set of labels from LB to LB+VBS-1. Each PE has a unique VE ID. A receiving PE adds its own VE ID to the label base to get the label to use toward the sender, so one update gives every peer a unique label. A VE block offset VBO lets a PE advertise several smaller blocks, which makes block management easier and lets it handle a new PE whose VE ID is not yet covered.

The VPLS NLRI uses the L2VPN AFI (25) and the VPLS SAFI (65). It holds a Length, an 8-octet Route Distinguisher, the VE ID, the VE Block Offset, the VE Block Size and a 3-octet Label Base.

When PE-b with VE ID W receives an announcement, it checks that VBO <= W < VBO + VBS. If so, the label to send to PE-a is LB + W - VBO. It also checks that it has announced a block covering the sender's VE ID, and makes a new announcement if not. If an NLRI is withdrawn, the PE MUST tear down its ends of the pseudowire.

The Layer2 Info Extended Community carries the Encaps Type (19 for VPLS), Control Flags and a Layer-2 MTU. The C flag says whether a control word MUST be present, and the S flag says whether sequenced delivery MUST be used. The remaining flag bits MUST be zero on send and ignored on receipt.
sections.eli5: Instead of mailing a separate key to each friend, you leave a numbered row of lockers. Each friend adds their own number to the first locker to find theirs.

sections.title: Multiple Networks, Multi-homing and Scale
sections.content:
If the sites of a VPLS attach to PEs in different Autonomous Systems, there is no I-BGP session between those PEs. The RFC gives three methods, in order of increasing scalability. In (a), the border routers (ASBRs) act as PEs and CEs to each other, which needs an Ethernet link, a VLAN sub-interface per VPLS and full VPLS state on the ASBRs. In (b), the ASBRs exchange VPLS NLRIs over E-BGP and swap labels, needing MPLS on the link but not Ethernet. In (c), a multi-hop E-BGP session runs between PEs or route reflectors, and the ASBRs hold no VPLS state at all.

A site can be multi-homed to several PEs. If the PEs use the same VE ID, BGP path selection builds a loop-free topology and the speaker MUST pick only one of the equivalent NLRIs. Such PEs MUST use the same Route Distinguisher. With different VE IDs, running Spanning Tree on the CE device is mandatory.

To avoid a full mesh of BGP sessions, the RFC uses BGP Route Reflectors, as in RFC 4456. These are purely a control plane technique and add no data plane state. Route Target Filtering limits updates to interested speakers.

A u-PE can do Layer 2 functions while its PE does the BGP work. How a PE and u-PE learn and forward is a local matter and is not signaled.
sections.eli5: If offices belong to different companies' networks, the helpers at the border have to pass notes along. There are three ways to do that, and the last way keeps the border helpers least busy.

sections.title: Forwarding Frames Like a Bridge
sections.content:
Frames from CEs are encapsulated as in RFC 4448. The whole provider network must look like a single logical learning bridge for each VPLS, so each VE learns source MAC addresses against logical ports, which are customer ports and pseudowires. If a MAC address shows up on a different port, the VE MUST update its table.

Entries should age out. Implementations SHOULD have an aging mechanism, and if the age exceeds the aging time T, the address MUST be flushed. A per-VPLS knob for T is a SHOULD.

A frame to an unknown destination is flooded to all other VEs in the VPLS. Broadcast frames are sent to all stations in the same way. Split horizon forwarding applies: a frame that arrived from another PE MUST NOT be sent on to other PEs, only to attached CEs, because the first PE has already sent it to all of them.

Learning can be unqualified (key is the MAC address) or qualified (customer VLAN tag plus MAC address). An implementation MAY map 802.1p bits to EXP bits for class of service.
sections.eli5: The network acts like a mail sorter. It remembers which door each name came from. If it does not know where a name lives, it asks every door, but it never forwards a note back to doors that were already asked.

sections.title: Privacy but Not Encryption
sections.content:
VPLS aims at data privacy: data in a VPLS reaches only other nodes in that VPLS. It does not offer confidentiality, integrity or authentication. Packets cross the provider network in the clear, so a man-in-the-middle can eavesdrop and may inject packets. If more is wanted, PE-to-PE tunnels can be IPsec tunnels, and end systems can encrypt before data enters the provider network.

Because all control exchanges use BGP, authenticating BGP sessions with the TCP MD5 option makes spoofed updates and withdraws harder. This does not keep VPLS labels private. Misconfiguration, such as associating the wrong Route Target with a VPLS, can connect CEs of different VPLSs and is left for further study.

For MPLS-in-IP and MPLS-in-GRE tunnels, an implementation MUST contain IPsec, and without it MUST let the egress PE validate the IP source address of tunneled packets.
sections.eli5: VPLS keeps different companies' mail in different bags, but the bags are not locked. If you want secrets kept, lock your own letters first.

fields.name: Route Distinguisher
fields.desc: 8 octets; unique per PE and VPLS if not configured.

fields.name: VE Block Offset
fields.desc: First VE ID covered by the label block.

fields.name: VE Block Size
fields.desc: Number of labels in the block.
